reason: POV reproduced before patching, no longer reproduced after patching, regressions passed, verifier accepted.

project.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

parsed_output.evidence: Unpatched run: shell argv[-1] = `echo 'a' ; touch /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker ; 'b'`, marker exists=true, RESULT: VULNERABLE, POV_EXIT=0. Simulated-patch run (removed the `source.startsWith(quoteChar) && source.endsWith(quoteChar)` shortcut in StringUtils.quoteAndEscape): shell argv[-1] = `echo ''\''a'\'' ; touch ... ; '\''b'\'''`, marker exists=false, RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE, POV_EXIT=1. Product code was restored afterward (git status shows NO_PRODUCT_CHANGES).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code the tainted argument "'a' ; touch /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker ; 'b'" passes through quoteAndEscape unchanged, so the rendered shell argv is `echo 'a' ; touch /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker ; 'b'`; Commandline.execute() runs it via /bin/sh -c, the embedded touch executes, the marker file is created, and the POV prints "RESULT: VULNERABLE" and exits 0. After a correct patch the argument is fully quoted/escaped (e.g. `echo ''\''a'\'' ; touch ... ; '\''b'\'''`), the touch runs as a literal argument to echo, no marker file is created, and the POV exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: The container is Linux so BourneShell/`/bin/sh -c` exercises the real execution path. The injected `echo` exits 141 (SIGPIPE) which is irrelevant; the POV's verdict is based solely on whether the injected `touch` created the marker file, making it deterministic. run_pov.sh compiles CommandInjectionPov.java against target/classes (building them first if absent) and runs it; the primary POV file is CommandInjectionPov.java.
parsed_output.regression_hint: A correct fix must ensure arguments/executables that already start and end with the quote delimiter are still escaped rather than trusted verbatim (i.e. remove/guard the pre-quoted shortcut in StringUtils.quoteAndEscape or force-escape shell metacharacters in Shell argument rendering). After the fix, `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` must exit non-zero and must not create /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real proof-of-vulnerability for CWE-078 OS command injection in plexus-utils. StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() (called from Shell.getRawCommandLine via Commandline.getShellCommandline/execute) returns any argument that already starts and ends with the shell's quote delimiter verbatim, skipping all neutralization. A BourneShell argument of the form "'a' ; touch <marker> ; 'b'" breaks out of the single quotes and injects an arbitrary command into the string handed to /bin/sh -c. The POV drives the real public API (new Commandline(new BourneShell()) -> setExecutable -> createArg().setValue -> execute()) and observes the injected `touch` creating a marker file. It exits 0 when the injection fires (unpatched) and exits 1 when neutralized (verified by temporarily removing the pre-quoted shortcut, which caused the arg to be fully escaped and the marker to not be created).

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() (the 6-arg escapePattern overload, reached from Shell.getRawCommandLine via Commandline.getShellCommandline/execute) short-circuited and returned `source` unchanged whenever it started and ended with the quote delimiter, skipping all neutralization. Attacker-controlled arguments beginning and ending with a single quote but containing interior quotes/metacharacters therefore passed through to /bin/sh -c verbatim.

Fix: replaced the unconditional pre-quoted shortcut with a guarded one. It still trusts an already-wrapped token, but for the single-quote delimiter it additionally requires that the delimiter appears only as the outer wrapper (source.indexOf('\'',1) == length-1). Malicious args with interior single quotes now fall through to escape()+wrap, producing '\''-style escaping that keeps the injected text as a literal argument. For non-single-quote delimiters the original behaviour is preserved, so BourneShell executable paths pre-quoted by unifyQuotes (which escapes interior double quotes as \") are not doubly quoted.

Considered but rejected: fully removing the shortcut (the exploiter's simulated patch). It neutralizes the POV but double-quotes the executable (unifyQuotes already wraps it), producing ""..."" and breaking testQuotedPathWithQuotationMark / testQuotedPathWithQuotationMarkAndApostrophe / testGetShellCommandLineBash_WithSingleQuotedArg. The delimiter-aware guard fixes the vuln while keeping all existing behaviour.

Added regression test testQuote_EscapeBrokenPreQuotedArgument asserting an interior-breakout single-quoted argument is fully escaped rather than returned verbatim.

Verification: POV (bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) now prints "RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE", exits 1, and creates no /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker. `mvn -B test` = 284 tests, 0 failures/0 errors.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only narrows which pre-quoted strings are trusted verbatim; it never loosens escaping. Behaviour for double-quote and other delimiters is unchanged, so executable-path quoting (including exotic paths containing quotes/spaces) is preserved, as confirmed by the full existing suite. The single-quote path now escapes any argument whose interior contains a single quote — a strict superset of neutralization vs. before, with no legitimate use case relying on interior-quote pass-through (POSIX single-quoted strings cannot contain single quotes anyway). Note: for the double-quote delimiter the shortcut still trusts pre-quoted tokens verbatim, so `$`/backtick inside a double-quoted executable path are not neutralized here — this is pre-existing behaviour for internally-generated executable paths and outside the scope of this argument-injection finding.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-078 OS command injection in plexus-utils by hardening StringUtils.quoteAndEscape(). The method previously returned any argument verbatim if it merely started and ended with the quote delimiter, so a BourneShell argument like "'a' ; touch <marker> ; 'b'" broke out of the single quotes and injected a command into the string passed to /bin/sh -c. The shortcut is now delimiter-aware: for the single-quote argument delimiter it only trusts a pre-quoted token when the delimiter never appears in the interior (a POSIX single-quoted string is fully literal and cannot contain even an escaped single quote), so any interior single quote forces full escaping. Other delimiters (e.g. the double-quote executable delimiter, whose interior quotes are backslash-escaped by BourneShell.unifyQuotes) keep the original behaviour, avoiding double-quoting of executable paths. The POV now exits 1 and creates no marker; the full test suite (284 tests) passes.

parsed_output.summary: The patch hardens StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() so an already-single-quoted argument containing interior single quotes is no longer trusted verbatim but fully escaped, closing the CWE-078 OS command injection in the Commandline/Shell rendering path. The POV no longer reproduces (exit 1, no marker file created) and all regression tests pass. The fix is minimal, targets the actual taint sink, does not modify or disable the POV, and removes no legitimate functionality.
